claim: Plant stem cells remain quiescent until the postembryonic phase of development, in contrast to most animals.
source: A major feature of embryogenesis is the specification of stem cell systems, but in contrast to the situation in most animals, plant stem cells remain quiescent until the postembryonic phase of development.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a general biological principle contrasting plant and animal development.

claim: Light is able to activate expression of the stem cell inducer WUSCHEL independently of photosynthesis.
source: We show on the one hand that light is able to activate expression of the stem cell inducer WUSCHEL independently of photosynthesis and that this likely involves inter-regional cytokinin signaling.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Light-dependent WUSCHEL activation likely involves inter-regional cytokinin signaling.
source: We show on the one hand that light is able to activate expression of the stem cell inducer WUSCHEL independently of photosynthesis and that this likely involves inter-regional cytokinin signaling.
evidence: This is stated as a likely mechanism based on experimental observations.

claim: Metabolic signals are transduced to the meristem through activation of the TARGET OF RAPAMYCIN (TOR) kinase.
source: Metabolic signals, on the other hand, are transduced to the meristem through activation of the TARGET OF RAPAMYCIN (TOR) kinase.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data.

claim: TOR is required for light signal dependent stem cell activation.
source: Surprisingly, TOR is also required for light signal dependent stem cell activation.
evidence: This is stated as a surprising finding in the abstract and supported by experimental data.

claim: The TOR kinase acts as a central integrator of light and metabolic signals for stem cell activation at the shoot apex.
source: Thus, the TOR kinase acts as a central integrator of light and metabolic signals and a key regulator of stem cell activation at the shoot apex.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the abstract, synthesizing the experimental findings.

claim: Light is the sole energy source of plants.
source: Light is the sole energy source of plants and therefore one of the most important environmental factors influencing their development and physiology.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Core developmental decisions during the plant lifecycle from germination to seedling development and flowering are strongly influenced by light conditions.
source: Consequently, several of the core developmental decisions during the lifecycle of a plant from germination to seedling development and flowering are strongly influenced by light conditions.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: After germination, higher plants undergo two distinct developmental programs depending on the availability of light, termed skotomorphogenesis and photomorphogenesis.
source: After germination, higher plants undergo two distinct developmental programs depending on the availability of light, termed skotomorphogenesis and photomorphogenesis.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Skotomorphogenesis is characterized by an etiolated phenotype, including an elongated hypocotyl, closed cotyledons, the formation of an apical hook and etioplast development.
source: Skotomorphogenesis, the dark adaptation program, is characterized by an etiolated phenotype, including an elongated hypocotyl, closed cotyledons, the formation of an apical hook and etioplast development.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Stem cells at the shoot and root tip remain dormant during skotomorphogenesis.
source: Importantly, stem cells at the shoot and root tip remain dormant and thus growth in etiolated seedlings is mainly dependent on cell elongation rather than cell division.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Growth in etiolated seedlings is mainly dependent on cell elongation rather than cell division.
source: Importantly, stem cells at the shoot and root tip remain dormant and thus growth in etiolated seedlings is mainly dependent on cell elongation rather than cell division.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Photomorphogenesis leads to seedlings with short hypocotyls, unfolded cotyledons and development of chloroplasts.
source: In contrast, photomorphogenesis, the developmental program triggered in light, leads to seedlings with short hypocotyls, unfolded cotyledons and development of chloroplasts.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: In the light, shoot and root meristems are activated, leading to root growth and development of the first leaves by cell division and expansion.
source: In the light, shoot and root meristems are activated, leading to root growth and development of the first leaves by cell division and expansion (reviewed in Nemhauser and Chory 2002).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation to a review.

claim: Photomorphogenesis is the default pathway based on evolutionary evidence.
source: Based on evolutionary evidence, photomorphogenesis is the default pathway, since gymnosperms for example do not follow a strict skotomorphogenic development in darkness (Wei, 1994).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to support the evolutionary argument.

claim: Gymnosperms do not follow a strict skotomorphogenic development in darkness.
source: Based on evolutionary evidence, photomorphogenesis is the default pathway, since gymnosperms for example do not follow a strict skotomorphogenic development in darkness (Wei, 1994).
evidence: This is stated with a citation as supporting evidence.

claim: The evolution of the dark-adapted skotomorphogenesis program ensued an advantage for land plants facing new environmental challenges.
source: With the advance of land plants and resulting new environmental challenges, such as growth in dense canopy and germination in soil, the evolution of the dark-adapted skotomorphogenesis program ensued an advantage: It allowed plants to allocate the limited energy sources supplied by the seed to maximally grow by elongation, in order to reach favorable light conditions that will provide energy for further growth and development.
evidence: This is stated as an evolutionary explanation based on established knowledge.

claim: Skotomorphogenesis allowed plants to allocate limited energy sources from the seed to maximally grow by elongation to reach favorable light conditions.
source: With the advance of land plants and resulting new environmental challenges, such as growth in dense canopy and germination in soil, the evolution of the dark-adapted skotomorphogenesis program ensued an advantage: It allowed plants to allocate the limited energy sources supplied by the seed to maximally grow by elongation, in order to reach favorable light conditions that will provide energy for further growth and development.
evidence: This is stated as an evolutionary explanation based on established knowledge.

claim: Plants have evolved complex mechanisms to perceive light quality and quantity through a range of photoreceptors that mainly absorb in the blue, red and far-red range of the spectrum.
source: To faithfully execute these opposing developmental programs, plants have evolved complex mechanisms to perceive light quality and quantity through a whole range of photoreceptors that are mainly absorbing in the blue, red and far-red range of the spectrum.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Activation of blue absorbing CRYPTOCHROMES and/or red and far-red absorbing PHYTOCHROMES overrides the skotomorphogenic program and plants undergo photomorphogenesis within minutes after perception of a light stimulus.
source: Activation of the blue absorbing CRYPTOCHROMES (crys) and/or the red and far-red absorbing PHYTOCHROMES (phys) overrides the skotomorphogenic program and plants undergo photomorphogenesis within minutes after perception of a light stimulus (reviewed in Chory, 2010).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation to a review.

claim: Activated light receptors inhibit the function of CONSTITUTIVE PHOTOMORPHOGENESIS 1 (COP1), an E3 ubiquitin ligase that targets positive regulators of photomorphogenesis for degradation in darkness.
source: On the molecular level, activated light receptors inhibit the function of the core repressor of photomorphogenesis, CONSTITUTIVE PHOTOMORPHOGENESIS 1 (COP1), an E3 ubiquitin ligase that targets positive regulators of photomorphogenesis for degradation in darkness (Yi and Deng, 2005).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: PHYTOCHROME INTERACTING FACTORS (PIFs), which promote skotomorphogenesis in darkness, are degraded upon light perception through the PHYTOCHROMES.
source: At the same time, a group of potent transcription factors, the PHYTOCHROME INTERACTING FACTORS (PIFs), which promote skotomorphogenesis in darkness, are degraded upon light perception through the PHYTOCHROMES (Leivar and Quail, 2010).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: The activities of COP1 and PIF pathways converge on the differential regulation of thousands of genes resulting in a massive reprogramming of the transcriptome in response to light.
source: The activities of these pathways converge on the differential regulation of thousands of genes resulting in a massive reprogramming of the transcriptome in response to light (Ma et al., 2002; Tepperman et al., 2004; Peschke and Kretsch, 2011; Pfeiffer et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with multiple citations.

claim: Light fuels photosynthesis and leads to the production of energy rich metabolites including sugars.
source: Light not only activates photoreceptors, it also fuels photosynthesis and therefore leads to the production of a number of energy rich metabolites including sugars.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Plants are able to monitor their metabolic state with several signaling systems.
source: Plants are able to monitor their metabolic state with several signaling systems (Lastdrager et al., 2014) and recent studies have focused on the evolutionary conserved TARGET OF RAPAMYCIN (TOR) kinase complex (Dobrenel et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: In other eukaryotes, TOR functions as a central integrator of nutrient, energy, and stress signaling networks.
source: In other eukaryotes, TOR functions as a central integrator of nutrient, energy, and stress signaling networks and consistently, TOR regulates cell growth and proliferation, ribosome biogenesis, protein synthesis, cell wall integrity and autophagy (Díaz-Troya et al., 2008; Henriques et al., 2014; Lastdragere et al., 2014; Xiong and Sheen, 2014).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with multiple citations.

claim: TOR regulates cell growth and proliferation, ribosome biogenesis, protein synthesis, cell wall integrity and autophagy.
source: In other eukaryotes, TOR functions as a central integrator of nutrient, energy, and stress signaling networks and consistently, TOR regulates cell growth and proliferation, ribosome biogenesis, protein synthesis, cell wall integrity and autophagy (Díaz-Troya et al., 2008; Henriques et al., 2014; Lastdragere et al., 2014; Xiong and Sheen, 2014).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with multiple citations.

claim: Other eukaryotes possess two TOR complexes, while only a single complex has been identified in plants so far.
source: While other eukaryotes possess two TOR complexes, so far only a single complex has been identified in plants.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: The plant TOR complex is comprised of TOR, FKBP12, LST8 and RAPTOR and resembles the mammalian TOR complex 1 (mTORC1).
source: It is comprised of TOR, FKBP12, LST8 and RAPTOR (Mahfouz et al., 2006; Moreau et al., 2012) and thus resembles the mammalian TOR complex 1 (mTORC1).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: AtTOR is expressed in the embryo and endosperm and in meristematic regions of the adult plant.
source: AtTOR is expressed in the embryo and endosperm and in meristematic regions of the adult plant (Menand et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated with a citation as established knowledge.

claim: tor null mutants show premature arrest of embryo development.
source: While tor null mutants show premature arrest of embryo development (Menand et al., 2002), knock down of TOR leads to growth reduction and affects the carbohydrate and amino acid metabolism (Caldana et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated with a citation as established knowledge.

claim: Knock down of TOR leads to growth reduction and affects the carbohydrate and amino acid metabolism.
source: While tor null mutants show premature arrest of embryo development (Menand et al., 2002), knock down of TOR leads to growth reduction and affects the carbohydrate and amino acid metabolism (Caldana et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated with a citation as established knowledge.

claim: The presence of sugars promotes TOR kinase activity.
source: In contrast, the presence of sugars in general promotes TOR kinase activity (Ren et al., 2012; Dobrenel et al., 2013; Xiong et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated with multiple citations as established knowledge.

claim: The only known direct downstream targets of AtTOR kinase are S6 kinase 1 (S6K1), TAP46, and E2 promoter binding factor a (E2Fa).
source: So far, the only known direct downstream targets of AtTOR kinase are S6 kinase 1 (S6K1) (Schepetilnikov et al., 2011, 2013; Xiong et al., 2013), TAP46 (Ahn et al., 2011, 2014) and E2 promoter binding factor a (E2Fa) (Xiong et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated with multiple citations as established knowledge.

claim: S6K1 plays an important role in reinitiating translation and in the regulation of the cell cycle.
source: S6K1 plays an important role in reinitiating translation (Schepetilnikov et al., 2011) as well as in the regulation of the cell cycle (Henriques et al., 2010; Shin et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated with citations as established knowledge.

claim: E2Fa is associated with cell cycle control through the expression of S-phase genes.
source: Similarly, E2Fa is associated with cell cycle control through the expression of S-phase genes (Polyn et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated with a citation as established knowledge.

claim: Little is known about how TOR is activated on a molecular level in plants.
source: Though little is known about how TOR is activated on a molecular level in plants, reports from the past decade suggest that TOR functions as a central regulator of protein synthesis, cell proliferation and metabolism in response to metabolic signals.
evidence: This is stated as a knowledge gap in the introduction.

claim: TOR functions as a central regulator of protein synthesis, cell proliferation and metabolism in response to metabolic signals.
source: Though little is known about how TOR is activated on a molecular level in plants, reports from the past decade suggest that TOR functions as a central regulator of protein synthesis, cell proliferation and metabolism in response to metabolic signals.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge based on recent reports.

claim: Several photomorphogenic responses can be triggered by a light signal alone, as displayed in dark-grown cop1 and pif1/pif3/pif4/pif5 quadruple mutants (pifq).
source: Several photomorphogenic responses, like the inhibition of hypocotyl elongation, unfolding of the hypocotyl hook and cotyledons, as well as chloroplast development can be triggered by a light signal alone, as displayed in dark-grown cop1 and pif1/pif3/pif4/pif5 quadruple mutants (pifq) (Deng and Quail, 1991; Leivar et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated with citations as established knowledge.

claim: Root growth is not induced in cop1 mutants unless sucrose is supplied with the growth medium.
source: However, root growth is not induced in cop1 mutants unless sucrose is supplied with the growth medium.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Photosynthetic assimilates dominantly promote growth in the root where they can synergistically interact with photoreceptor-triggered light signaling.
source: Photosynthetic assimilates dominantly promote growth in the root where they can synergistically interact with photoreceptor-triggered light signaling (Kircher and Schopfer, 2012).
evidence: This is stated with a citation as established knowledge.

claim: Photosynthesis-driven growth and proliferation in the root is mediated by the TOR kinase.
source: Recently, Xiong et al. showed that this photosynthesis-driven growth and proliferation in the root is mediated by the TOR kinase (Xiong et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated with a citation as established knowledge.

claim: Stem cell control in the SAM of Arabidopsis thaliana is based on the activity of the homeodomain transcription factor WUSCHEL (WUS).
source: Stem cell control in the SAM of Arabidopsis thaliana is based on the activity of the homeodomain transcription factor WUSCHEL (WUS), which is expressed in the organizing centre and necessary and sufficient to non-cell- autonomously induce stem cell fate by protein movement.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: WUS is expressed in the organizing centre and is necessary and sufficient to non-cell-autonomously induce stem cell fate by protein movement.
source: Stem cell control in the SAM of Arabidopsis thaliana is based on the activity of the homeodomain transcription factor WUSCHEL (WUS), which is expressed in the organizing centre and necessary and sufficient to non-cell- autonomously induce stem cell fate by protein movement.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Stem cells express CLAVATA3 (CLV3), a short secreted peptide, that acts via the CLV / CORYNE receptor system to limit the expression of WUS in the organizing center.
source: Stem cells in turn express CLAVATA3 (CLV3), a short secreted peptide, that acts via the CLV / CORYNE receptor system to limit the expression of WUS in the organizing center (Schoof et al., 2000; Daum et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated with citations as established knowledge.

claim: Supplementation of sugar to wild-type seedlings grown in the dark is inefficient to trigger development.
source: While supplementation of sugar to wild-type seedlings grown in the dark is known to be inefficient to trigger development (Figure 1A), activation of the light pathway alone, either physiologically by low level illumination, or genetically by introduction of the cop1 mutation, was shown to induce photomorphogenic development of the hypocotyl and cotyledons in darkness (Deng and Quail, 1991).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 1A and a citation.

claim: Activation of the light pathway alone induces photomorphogenic development of the hypocotyl and cotyledons in darkness.
source: While supplementation of sugar to wild-type seedlings grown in the dark is known to be inefficient to trigger development (Figure 1A), activation of the light pathway alone, either physiologically by low level illumination, or genetically by introduction of the cop1 mutation, was shown to induce photomorphogenic development of the hypocotyl and cotyledons in darkness (Deng and Quail, 1991).
evidence: This is stated with a citation as established knowledge.

claim: SAMs of cop1 mutants were unable to produce organs when grown in the dark.
source: Despite this stark developmental transition, SAMs of cop1 mutants were unable to produce organs when grown in the dark.
evidence: This is stated as an experimental observation in the Results section.

claim: The SAM was activated and organogenesis initiated in 100% of the dark-grown cop1 mutants when supplemented with sucrose as external energy source.
source: However, the SAM was activated and organogenesis initiated in 100% of the dark-grown cop1 mutants when supplemented with sucrose as external energy source (Figure 1B, see also McNellis et al., 1994; Nakagawa and Komeda, 2004).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental observation with reference to Figure 1B and citations.

claim: The SAM of light-grown wild-type seedlings remained dormant when photosynthesis was compromised by the carotenoid biosynthesis inhibitor norflurazon.
source: Conversely, the SAM of light-grown wild-type seedlings remained dormant when photosynthesis was compromised by the carotenoid biosynthesis inhibitor norflurazon.
evidence: This is stated as an experimental observation in the Results section.

claim: Supplementing the growth medium of norflurazon-treated plants with sucrose rescued the dormant phenotype in approximately every third seedling.
source: In line with our observation of cop1 mutants, supplementing the growth medium of these plants with sucrose rescued the dormant phenotype in approximately every third seedling (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental observation with reference to Figure 1C.

claim: Neither the availability of energy metabolites, nor light perception alone was sufficient for SAM activation.
source: Thus, neither the availability of energy metabolites, nor light perception alone was sufficient for SAM activation.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the experimental observations.

claim: Light and energy, likely in the form of photosynthetic products, are sensed independently, and both factors need to act cooperatively to trigger SAM development.
source: In contrast, light and energy, likely in the form of photosynthetic products, seemed to be sensed independently, and both factors need to act cooperatively to trigger SAM development.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the experimental observations.

claim: Stem cell identity was actively maintained independently of growth conditions and was even observed in the dormant state mediated by germination in the dark.
source: By using transcriptional reporters for stem cells (pCLV3:mCherry-NLS) and niche cells (pWUS:3xVENUS-NLS) we found that stem cell identity was actively maintained independently of growth conditions and was even observed in the dormant state mediated by germination in the dark (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental observation with reference to Figure 1D.

claim: Expression of the WUS transcription factor reporter was critically dependent on environmental signals and preceded meristem activity and the initiation of organogenic development.
source: In contrast, expression of the reporter for the stem cell inducing WUS transcription factor was critically dependent on environmental signals and preceded meristem activity and the initiation of organogenic development (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental observation with reference to Figure 1E.

claim: In situ hybridization confirmed strong light dependent induction of WUS mRNA.
source: To test if our WUS reporter faithfully recapitulated the behavior of the endogenous gene, we used in situ hybridization and were able to confirm strong light dependent induction of WUS mRNA (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C and D).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental observation with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1C and D.

claim: WUS-GFP protein showed strong light- and sucrose-dependency in line with the observed activation of the WUS promoter and accumulation of the endogenous WUS mRNA.
source: Again, we observed a strong light- and sucrose-dependency of the WUS-GFP signal in line with the observed activation of the WUS promoter and accumulation of the endogenous WUS mRNA under these conditions (Figure 1G–I) confirming that the simple pWUS:3xVenus-NLS reporter represents a faithful and quantitative readout for WUS activity.
evidence: This is stated as an experimental observation with reference to Figure 1G–I.

claim: The pWUS:3xVenus-NLS reporter represents a faithful and quantitative readout for WUS activity.
source: Again, we observed a strong light- and sucrose-dependency of the WUS-GFP signal in line with the observed activation of the WUS promoter and accumulation of the endogenous WUS mRNA under these conditions (Figure 1G–I) confirming that the simple pWUS:3xVenus-NLS reporter represents a faithful and quantitative readout for WUS activity.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the experimental observations.

claim: CLV3 expression is at least partially independent of WUS.
source: Taken together, these findings on the one hand suggested that CLV3 expression is at least partially independent of WUS and on the other hand that the environmentally dependent transcriptional activation of WUS is the trigger to overcome stem cell dormancy.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the experimental observations.

claim: The environmentally dependent transcriptional activation of WUS is the trigger to overcome stem cell dormancy.
source: Taken together, these findings on the one hand suggested that CLV3 expression is at least partially independent of WUS and on the other hand that the environmentally dependent transcriptional activation of WUS is the trigger to overcome stem cell dormancy.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the experimental observations.

claim: The WUS reporter (pWUS:3xVENUS-NLS) was below detection level in dark-grown seedlings.
source: Using seedlings carrying both reporters grown under wave-length specific LED illumination and image quantification we found that the WUS reporter (pWUS:3xVENUS-NLS) was below detection level in dark-grown seedlings.
evidence: This is stated as an experimental observation in the Results section.

claim: GFP signals from the WUS reporter were readily detectable in light-grown plants from three days after germination onwards with the signal steadily increasing over time.
source: In contrast, GFP signals were readily detectable in light-grown plants from three days after germination onwards with the signal steadily increasing over time (Figure 1J).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental observation with reference to Figure 1J.

claim: WUS expression was induced in the absence of light when plants were grown on sucrose-supplemented medium.
source: Interestingly, WUS expression was also induced in the absence of light, when plants were grown on sucrose-supplemented medium (Figure 1F,J) and when sucrose was supplied to light-grown seedlings, the effect of light and sucrose on WUS expression was additive (Figure 1J).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental observation with reference to Figure 1F,J.

claim: When sucrose was supplied to light-grown seedlings, the effect of light and sucrose on WUS expression was additive.
source: Interestingly, WUS expression was also induced in the absence of light, when plants were grown on sucrose-supplemented medium (Figure 1F,J) and when sucrose was supplied to light-grown seedlings, the effect of light and sucrose on WUS expression was additive (Figure 1J).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental observation with reference to Figure 1J.

claim: Light and sucrose had a similar effect on the regulation of CLV3 expression.
source: Light and sucrose also had a similar effect on the regulation of CLV3 expression (Figure 1D–I, K), however, since the CLV3 reporter was already detectable in dark-grown seedlings, the induction of expression by light and sucrose was less pronounced and mainly due to an enlargement of the CLV3 domain rather than an increase of signal intensity in individual cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental observation with reference to Figure 1D–I, K and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: The induction of CLV3 expression by light and sucrose was mainly due to an enlargement of the CLV3 domain rather than an increase of signal intensity in individual cells.
source: Light and sucrose also had a similar effect on the regulation of CLV3 expression (Figure 1D–I, K), however, since the CLV3 reporter was already detectable in dark-grown seedlings, the induction of expression by light and sucrose was less pronounced and mainly due to an enlargement of the CLV3 domain rather than an increase of signal intensity in individual cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental observation with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: Development of the SAM required both light signal transduction and the availability of photosynthetic products.
source: In sum, development of the SAM required both, light signal transduction and the availability of photosynthetic products, whereas WUS expression was induced also by each signal individually.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the experimental observations.

claim: WUS expression was induced by light signal transduction or availability of photosynthetic products individually.
source: In sum, development of the SAM required both, light signal transduction and the availability of photosynthetic products, whereas WUS expression was induced also by each signal individually.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the experimental observations.

claim: Blue and red light at low intensities were sufficient to robustly induce WUS expression.
source: Even at low intensities, blue, as well as red light were sufficient to robustly induce WUS expression (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental observation with reference to Figure 2A.

claim: Red-light-induced WUS activation was specifically reduced in the phyB mutant background.
source: In line with the well-documented biochemistry of the photoreceptors, red-light-induced WUS activation was specifically reduced in the phyB mutant background, while blue-light-induced reporter activity was impaired in the cry1/cry2 double mutant background (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental observation with reference to Figure 2A.

claim: Blue-light-induced WUS reporter activity was impaired in the cry1/cry2 double mutant background.
source: In line with the well-documented biochemistry of the photoreceptors, red-light-induced WUS activation was specifically reduced in the phyB mutant background, while blue-light-induced reporter activity was impaired in the cry1/cry2 double mutant background (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental observation with reference to Figure 2A.

claim: Light perceived through phyB and the crys influences the developmental fate of the SAM.
source: We thus concluded that light perceived through phyB as well as the crys influences the developmental fate of the SAM.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the experimental observations.

claim: WUS promoter activity was only weakly induced by far-red light.
source: We also tested WUS expression under far-red light, which is sensed by phyA and found that reporter activity was only weakly induced by far-red light.
evidence: This is stated as an experimental observation in the Results section.

claim: phyA mutants showed similar WUS promoter activity under far-red light and in darkness.
source: Interestingly, phyA mutants showed similar WUS promoter activity under far-red light and in darkness (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental observation with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: When growth media was supplemented with 1% sucrose, a clear induction of WUS expression was observed in response to far-red light, which was dependent on a functional copy of PHYA.
source: However, when we supplemented the growth media with 1% sucrose we observed a clear induction of WUS expression in response to far-red light, which was dependent on a functional copy of PHYA.
evidence: This is stated as an experimental observation in the Results section.

claim: phyA mutants displayed a basal level of WUS promoter activity in darkness when grown on plates containing sucrose.
source: Still, phyA mutants displayed a basal level of WUS promoter activity already in darkness even when grown on plates containing sucrose, suggesting a complex and so far unknown regulatory role for phyA under these conditions.
evidence: This is stated as an experimental observation in the Results section.

claim: phyA has a complex and so far unknown regulatory role in WUS expression under sucrose conditions.
source: Still, phyA mutants displayed a basal level of WUS promoter activity already in darkness even when grown on plates containing sucrose, suggesting a complex and so far unknown regulatory role for phyA under these conditions.
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the experimental observations.

claim: The inhibition of photosynthesis by either norflurazon or lincomycin did not affect WUS promoter activity in red or in blue light.
source: However, the inhibition of photosynthesis by either norflurazon or lincomycin, did not affect WUS promoter activity in red or in blue light (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental observation with reference to Figure 2A.

claim: In the presence of lincomycin, WUS expression was slightly increased under both red and blue light conditions.
source: In the presence of lincomycin, WUS expression was even slightly increased under both light conditions.
evidence: This is stated as an experimental observation in the Results section.

claim: WUS induction by red light was unaffected by CO2 reduction in the atmosphere.
source: Importantly, WUS induction by red light was unaffected by CO2 reduction in the atmosphere (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental observation with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Photosynthetically derived metabolites produced in a low light environment were not required for activation of stem cells.
source: Thus, photosynthetically derived metabolites produced in a low light environment were not required for activation of stem cells, confirming that light signaling alone was sufficient for WUS expression.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the experimental observations.

claim: Light signaling alone was sufficient for WUS expression.
source: Thus, photosynthetically derived metabolites produced in a low light environment were not required for activation of stem cells, confirming that light signaling alone was sufficient for WUS expression.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the experimental observations.

claim: Cop1-4 mutants displayed photomorphogenic development in darkness, which was accompanied by WUS expression.
source: Cop1-4 mutants displayed photomorphogenic development in darkness, which was accompanied by WUS expression (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental observation with reference to Figure 2B.

claim: The repressive function of COP1 on WUS expression was prominent under all conditions tested.
source: Furthermore, the repressive function of COP1 was prominent under all conditions tested and cop1-4 seedlings displayed strongly elevated WUS promoter activity compared to wild-type when grown in dark with or without sugar, and also under low light conditions (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental observation with reference to Figure 2B.

claim: cop1-4 seedlings displayed strongly elevated WUS promoter activity compared to wild-type when grown in dark with or without sugar, and also under low light conditions.
source: Furthermore, the repressive function of COP1 was prominent under all conditions tested and cop1-4 seedlings displayed strongly elevated WUS promoter activity compared to wild-type when grown in dark with or without sugar, and also under low light conditions (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental observation with reference to Figure 2B.

claim: All three cop1 mutant alleles tested showed robust elevation of WUS mRNA levels when grown in the dark.
source: Importantly, all three cop1 mutant alleles tested showed robust elevation of WUS mRNA levels when grown in the dark (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E), demonstrating that loss of COP1 function leads to activation of WUS.
evidence: This is stated as an experimental observation with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Loss of COP1 function leads to activation of WUS.
source: Importantly, all three cop1 mutant alleles tested showed robust elevation of WUS mRNA levels when grown in the dark (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E), demonstrating that loss of COP1 function leads to activation of WUS.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the experimental observations with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 1E.

claim: hy5 mutants were unaffected in activation of WUS expression.

claim: Stem cell fate as defined by CLV3 promoter activity can exist without WUS in a physiologically and developmentally relevant setting.
source: Since WUS protein exhibits complex movement and a short lifetime (Daum et al., 2014), we furthermore analyzed the behavior of WUS-GFP protein in vivo by recording the GFP signal in our rescue line (pWUS:WUS-linker-GFP in wus mutant background [Daum et al., 2014]). Again, we observed a strong light- and sucrose-dependency of the WUS-GFP signal in line with the observed activation of the WUS promoter and accumulation of the endogenous WUS mRNA under these conditions (Figure 1G–I) confirming that the simple pWUS:3xVenus-NLS reporter represents a faithful and quantitative readout for WUS activity. Taken together, these findings on the one hand suggested that CLV3 expression is at least partially independent of WUS and on the other hand that the environmentally dependent transcriptional activation of WUS is the trigger to overcome stem cell dormancy.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the experimental observations.
